events.title: ¡Puro Ritmo! The Musical Journey of Salsa
events.venue: Molina Family Latino Gallery at the National Museum of American History
events.description: From the streets of Havana to the dancefloors of New York and beyond, "¡Puro Ritmo!" explores how Afro-Cuban music evolved into a defining sound in the U.S. This bilingual exhibition traces salsa’s roots and rise through nearly 300 objects. Highlighting artists from Tito Puente and Celia Cruz to local legends and hidden pioneers, "¡Puro Ritmo!" celebrates salsa as one of America’s great musical traditions. A centerpiece of the exhibition is the presentation of five ensembles and five pairs of shoes worn by Celia Cruz, celebrated worldwide as the Queen of Salsa. Gifted by the Estate of Celia Cruz, the five dresses and a pair of shoes are now part of the Latino Museum’s permanent collection. The outfits will rotate throughout the exhibition’s two-and-a-half-year run, offering visitors multiple opportunities to experience Cruz’s vibrant stage presence.In addition to Cruz, the exhibition highlights iconic figures such as Tito Puente and Eddie Palmieri, as well as influential artists including Arsenio Rodríguez, Graciela, Ray Barretto and Willie Colón. It also explores the industry-shaping impact of Fania Records and its cofounders, Jerry Masucci and Johnny Pacheco.

events.title: “In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness”
events.description: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History will lead the nation’s 250th anniversary celebrations with a bold, immersive exhibition exploring the ideals of the Declaration of Independence. “In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness,” will open May 14, featuring 250 objects, across 250,000 square feet of the museum’s three public floors, including the desk Jefferson used to draft the Declaration of Independence. Another noteworthy Revolutionary War artifact is the only surviving ship of the early U.S. Navy, the gunboat Philadelphia. This National Historic Landmark helped stall British forces and now will undergo an on-site conservation to preserve it for future generations. A favorite with visitors is the Star-Spangled Banner the 1813 flag that inspired the National Anthem. A free guide will be available to help locate the artifacts, which range from the 1700s to the 21st century. The museum will also offer an extensive website to online visitors and those who want to take a deeper dive into this history following their visit. Visitors and online audiences can engage with both the triumphs and challenges of America’s journey through a series of dynamic programs, from hands-on activities and theatrical performances to educational tools and virtual field trips for classrooms across the country. The museum's Semiquincentennial exhibitions and events will welcome all Americans to reflect and commemorate on this significant anniversary. It closes in December 2026.

events.title: A Christmas Carol
events.description: Charles Dickens’s timeless tale of redemption takes on a music-filled, theatrical life in this stage adaptation of A Christmas Carol. events.title: A Sherlock Carol
events.description: A Sherlock Carol , a play with carols, by Mark Shanahan inspired by the works of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, is an inventive holiday production that seamlessly intertwines the worlds of Sherlock Holmes and A Christmas Carol. Set in 1894, the story reimagines a grown-up Tiny Tim who seeks out the famed detective to investigate the mysterious death of Ebenezer Scrooge. Holmes is compelled to confront his own past and inner turmoil, guided by spectral encounters reminiscent of Scrooge’s transformative journey. Combining aspects of two classics of Victorian literature and uniting them both in a joyful mug of holiday cheer, this play is a festive feast for the senses. Recommended for ages 6 & up.

events.title: All The World's A Stage
events.description: Visit Signature Theatre to see All The World's A Stage! A moving new musical about embracing who you are and the life-saving power of art by one of contemporary musical theater’s most exciting voices Adam Gwon (Ordinary Days, Cake Off). In 1996, a closeted high school math teacher agrees to mentor a student for a theater competition. Both outsiders in their small-town community, their exploration of Angels in America unsettles the town’s delicate balance, and the vise of intolerance begins to tighten, twisting their lives in unexpected ways. This deeply human tale, with a vibrantly expressive score, is a rallying cry for authenticity and a touching tribute to all the teachers whose selfless courage uplifts and changes us all.

events.description: Old Glory, reimagined: artists transform our flag over the centuries. Across generations, the Stars and Stripes has inspired pride, protest, and profound artistic expression. events.title: Are You Now or Have You Ever Been?
events.venue: Arena Stage at the Mead Center for American Theater
events.description: Straight from Off-Broadway comes Eric Bentley's timely American docudrama, Are You Now or Have You Ever Been?, directed by Tony Award winner Anna D. Shapiro. This electrifying story drops you into the tense world of the 1940s House Un-American Activities Committee hearings, where fame offered no protection and political pressure could end a career. Using the original transcripts, the play features the words of artists like Arthur Miller, Jerome Robbins, Paul Robeson, Elia Kazan, Lillian Hellman, Abe Burrows, and Lionel Stander as they faced impossible choices: defend their integrity, protect their careers, or betray their peers. And yet the probing, chilling questions posed by the committee are as powerful as the testimonies themselves, revealing a climate of intimidation and moral conflict that resonates far beyond its time.

events.title: Avery, Gottlieb & Rothko: By the Sea
events.description: Discover the story of the enduring friendship between three towering figures in American art: Milton Avery (1885–1965), Adolph Gottlieb (1903–1974), and Mark Rothko (1903–1970). This exhibition highlights the inspiration they derived from summers in Gloucester, Massachusetts, on Cape Ann, and beyond. Through approximately 90 paintings, drawings, and watercolors from the 1920s to the mid-1960s, this exhibition reflects in depth for the first time on the artistic exchange between these three artists, the experiences they shared, and the support they gave one another. Many works have never been on public view. IMAGE: Milton Avery, Black Sea, 1959, The Phillips Collection, Acquired 1965; © 2025 Milton Avery Trust/Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York

events.title: Bison: Standing Strong
events.address: 10th St. & Constitution Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20560
events.description: Explore the remarkable story of bison. These iconic animals shaped North American landscapes for more than 100,000 years and anchored Indigenous lifeways for generations. Pushed to the brink of extinction in the 19th century, bison survived thanks to dedicated conservation efforts. Today, they stand strong as an enduring symbol of survival and resilience. The Bison: Standing Strong exhibit invites you into this incredible journey. Explore a full-sized bull bison specimen, the six-foot-wide skull of an ancient bison ancestor, an immersive soundscape, multimedia, cutting-edge scientific research, and Native objects and stories shared in collaboration with community members. Experience the deep history of America’s national mammal and discover the hopeful future being built for generations to come.

events.title: Bronze Bison: Exhibit
events.address: 10th St. & Constitution Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20560
events.description: More than 100 years ago, real bison grazed outside the Smithsonian Castle building. Bison are returning in a bold new way! Three larger-than-life bronze bison, created by sculptor Gary Staab, find a permanent home outside the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History. These towering sculptures of a bull, cow, and calf are at 125 percent scale and modeled after taxidermy specimens seen at the Smithsonian between 1888 and 1957. The original bison diorama introduced generations of visitors to an animal and a prairie landscape they had never seen and helped spark the bison conservation movement. The new bison bronzes will welcome visitors from around the world and celebrate America’s national mammal. Gift of Naoma Tate and the family of Hal Tate.

events.title: Capitol Hill & Library of Congress Walking Tour
events.description: Enjoy a "Top of The Hill" experience touring Capitol Hill on a guided walking tour including a stop outside of the Supreme Court and entry tickets to the Library of Congress and the US Capitol. We tour inside the Library of Congress and US Capitol. (During government shutdown, this tour runs as usual but we will not enter any closed federal buildings. We will enter any buildings that remain open) Immerse yourself in the sights of Washington, DC on a guided walking tour. Enjoy entry tickets to the Library of Congress and Capitol Building. View the Supreme Court building and walk on Capitol Hill and learn about the country's legislative and judicial branches. Begin your tour at the top of "the Hill" and hear fascinating anecdotes and facts about the country's legal system. Originally named Jenkins Hill, find out how this area quickly expanded to become the epicenter of American government and politics. Walk by the Supreme Court building, known as "The Marble Palace", and the surrounding Congressional office buildings. Tour inside the Library of Congress, the national library of the United States, and the oldest federal cultural institution in the country. Proceed to the Capitol Building to marvel at its neoclassical style and iconic architecture, while your guide details its rich history. Before concluding your tour, your guide will bring you into the US Capitol Visitor Center to arrange for your tour of the capitol.

events.title: Cocoa, Cookies & Cows | A Highland Cow + Valais Sheep  Holiday Experience
events.description: Cocoa, Cookies & Cows | A Highland Cow + Valais Sheep Holiday Experience One of Scarlet Springs Farm’s most beloved holiday traditions is back! Cocoa, Cookies & Cows invites you to spend a festive afternoon with our adorable Highland cows, calves, Valais sheep, and lambs before warming up with homemade hot cocoa and cookies in our beautifully decorated Ridgetop Stable. Your experience begins with a 30-minute group animal immersion, where you’ll have the chance to pet, brush, feed, and love on our friendly Highland cows and calves, along with our famously puppy-dog-friendly Valais sheep and lambs. While the animals don’t mind sharing their barn, this portion of the experience will be largely outdoors, so please dress accordingly. After enjoying the highlands & lambs, we’ll clean up and then head down to the Ridgetop Stable, where you can warm up in our heated, enclosed space for the remaining hour while taking in the sweeping views of the farm. For the holidays, the stable will be transformed with festive décor and music to create the perfect cozy holiday setting. Settle in with your family, sip on homemade hot cocoa, enjoy a tower of delicious cookies, and soak up what makes Scarlet Springs so special. Before you head home, be sure to stop by The Scarlet Shop for Highland-inspired Christmas gifts and keepsakes. Whether this is your first visit or an annual family tradition, Cocoa, Cookies & Cows is the perfect way to slow down, get cozy, and make holiday memories together.​ ​What’s Included with Your Ticket: 1.5 hour experience on the beautiful 74-acre Scarlet Springs Far 30 minutes with the Highlands — pet, brush, feed, and meet our fluffy, friendly Highland cows and calves Time with our Valais sheep and lambs Seat with your party in our festive, beautifully decorated and heated Ridgetop Stable Homemade hot cocoa and cookies Sweeping views of the farm and a festive holiday atmosphere

events.description: Crazy Chester Formed in early 2020 for a series of one-off events in the piedmont region of North Carolina, Crazy Chester is a homegrown tribute act to The Band, consisting of Carrboro musicians Jones Bell (Mellow Swells, Ravary), Charles Cleaver (Big Star's Third, Fancy Gap, Lemon Sparks), Rob DiMauro (Heat Preacher, Mixtape Grab Bag, One After 919), Justin Ellis (Slow Teeth, Ravary, Easter Island, One After 919), and Rafael Green (solo artist, Ravary, One After 919), respectively recreating and playing the parts of Richard Manuel, Garth Hudson, Levon Helm, Rick Danko, and Robbie Robertson. But this time - they're taking the show on the road to celebrate 50 Years of The Last Waltz. A show that must be seen to be believed. Full list of guest performers TBD!

events.address: Dupont Circle NW, Washington, DC 20036, Washington DC, 20036
events.description: If you enjoy historical stories of conspiracy, politics, cover-ups, and assassinations, this tour is for you. Join Spyher, the #1 D.C. Walking Spy Tours provider, for the Embassy Row Spy Tour, led by a former CIA officer. This immersive 90-minute walking tour begins at the Dupont Circle Fountain and ends near the Dupont Circle Hotel, guiding guests through one of Washington, D.C.’s most storied corridors of diplomacy and espionage. Along Massachusetts Avenue, examine the suspicious death of a Kremlin insider and learn how Russian intelligence has used strategy, communication, and cover to operate in plain sight. Dive into the origins of Embassy Row and explore real case studies of infamous traitors and defectors who lived and worked nearby, including Jonathan Pollard and “Merry” Fahrney. Learn what motivates spies to betray their countries and how intelligence successes and failures shaped history. Guests will also conduct a hands-on secret operation along the route. Hint: bring your map-reading skills. This experience blends real intelligence history, intrigue, and interactive elements, making it ideal for date nights, couples, locals, and visitors seeking a unique way to explore D.C.’s past.

events.title: Embassy Row Walking Tour
events.description: Learn about the people and places that have turned this district into one of the most exclusive neighborhoods in the city and the center of the foreign diplomatic community. Walk around the world and see the international side of the nation’s capital city. Massachusetts Avenue is home to a dazzling array of international diplomatic missions, each embassy offering a glimpse into their country’s culture and heritage. These buildings not only host diplomatic affairs but also offer events that celebrate their respective nations’ rich histories and traditions. A historic private club dating back to 1878, the Cosmos Club is housed in a majestic mansion that exudes sophistication. Anderson House, a marvel of early 20th-century design, was once the winter residence of Larz and Isabel Anderson. Today, it serves as the headquarters of the Society of the Cincinnati. Nestled in the Kalorama neighborhood, the Woodrow Wilson House is a lovingly preserved time capsule of the former president’s life. This historic site features period furnishings, personal artifacts, and educational displays about Wilson’s presidency and legacy. A hidden gem in the city, the Spanish Steps provides a quiet and picturesque escape from the urban bustle. Modeled after the famous steps in Rome, this charming staircase is surrounded by lush greenery and historic homes. events.title: Friends Gather Here: A Legacy of Two Communities at Woodlawn
events.description: Friends Gather Here: A Legacy of Two Communities at Woodlawn explores the powerful history of Quaker families who came to Woodlawn to establish an antislavery community rooted in equality and nonviolence. Through innovative farming and free labor, they sought to demonstrate an alternative to slavery in Virginia, settling alongside a small, established free Black community already living in the area. This exhibit examines the parallel lives, shared aspirations, and evolving relationships between these neighboring communities. As part of the Virginia 250th commemoration, Friends Gather Here invites us to reflect on this quiet revolution and examine our nation’s foundational ideals. events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.description: Historic Blenheim is famous for its graffiti! Blenheim is an attractive c.1859 brick farmhouse perched atop a grassy hill. Exhibits, and the daily guided tour of the Historic Blenheim house, focus on the impact of war in the area, the family, and enslaved residents of Blenheim, and the Union soldiers that left their mark as they traveled through Fairfax Courthouse. Multimedia in our large viewing room shows specific features of the house’s walls. Walk the 12-acre grounds and view interpretive signage along groomed pathways. No visit is complete without a stop at the Willcoxon family cemetery. The house and surrounding 12 acres of former farmland offer an attractive backdrop for your vacation photos. events.address: 14th Street and Constitution Avenue, N.W., Washington, DC 20560
events.description: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History will lead the nation’s 250th anniversary celebrations with a bold, immersive exhibition exploring the ideals of the Declaration of Independence. In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness will span three floors and 300,000 square feet, featuring 250 significant objects, including the desk Jefferson used to draft the Declaration of Independence. Another noteworthy artifact is the only surviving ship of the early U.S. Navy, the gunboat Philadelphia . This National Historic Landmark helped stall British forces and now will undergo an on-site conservation to preserve it for future generations. Visitors and online audiences can engage with both the triumphs and challenges of America’s journey through a year-long series of dynamic programs, from hands-on activities and theatrical performances to educational tools and virtual field trips for classrooms across the country. The museum's Semiquincentennial exhibitions and events begin in the spring of 2026, welcoming all Americans to reflect on the enduring and sometimes delayed or denied promises that surround the ongoing pursuit of life, liberty and happiness.

events.title: Interwoven: A Tradition of Textiles
events.description: Textiles have long served as both functional objects and extraordinary works of art, woven into the fabric of everyday life and elevated by generations of makers. Hillwood's upcoming exhibition will be the first to focus on this essential yet unexplored aspect of the collection, showcasing the remarkable artistry, technical mastery, and cultural importance of textiles across centuries. Drawing from Hillwood's rich holdings, the exhibition invites visitors to consider the enduring power of textiles, not only as decorative or domestic objects but also as expressions of identity, devotion, innovation, and exquisite craftsmanship. Marjorie Merriweather Post's Collection Marjorie Merriweather Post maintained a reverence for textiles throughout her life, preserving antique lace samples, apparel from her girlhood, and examples of textile work created by the women in her family, including her mother, Ella Letitia Merriweather (1853-1912); her paternal aunt, Mary "Mollie" Stanley Post (1860-1925); and her grandmother, Caroline Lathrop Post (1824-1915). Post applied the same criteria to textiles as she did all her collecting: exquisite artisanship and intricate details. She collected handmade lace pieces and resplendent liturgical vestments and textiles from the Russian Orthodox Church, furnished her homes and personal spaces with sumptuous fabrics, and attired herself and her three daughters in the finest of fashions. Post also maintained a progressive approach to repurposing textiles, such as snipping embroidered sections of a daytime ensemble for an alternate use and upholstering chairs with an antique quilt. Textiles on View Organized into four sections, the exhibition will explore centuries' worth of historical textiles; the act of creating such fiber-based pieces; form and function, including lace, embroidery and needlepoint, and quilts and coverings; and commemorative textiles, which serve as relics of the past. events.title: Miguel Braceli: UNBURIAL (exhibition)
events.address: St. John's College, 60 College Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21401
events.description: Unburial treats absence as a site for learning and reflection. The void left by the Liberty Tree becomes more than metaphor: an art intervention transforms it into a place to be repurposed and reclaimed through rituals and celebrations that probe what freedom means today. On the front lawn, where the Liberty Tree once stood, the artist Miguel Braceli has installed a 40'-diameter circle of cemetery vases filled with common wildflowers. It calls attention to the tree's absence and reclaims it as a tree for all people, not just the privileged and elite (e.g., the Sons of Liberty and the four Annapolis signers of the Declaration of Independence). In the museum, Braceli, with the help of a team of fabricators, created three enormous murals and two other works. The murals perform an autopsy of the tree. The largest multiplies the tulip poplar's distinctive leaf shape across a 33'-long wall in a wind-swept swirl of energy (the leaves were made from stencils of the Liberty Tree scion's actual leaves). A second mural abstracts the tree's tangled root system into a water-bearing drawing (using PVC tubing) that sprouts purple carnations. The third mural's subject is the tree's massive trunk, which was cut to pieces in 1999, with much of the wood later finding commemorative as Liberty Tree guitars, conference tables, and bible boxes. Onto nine chalkboards, Braceli has mounted nine pieces of raw wood, each supporting live orchids. What can we learn anew from this tree?, it seems to ask. The two other works urge us to turn away from nation-state identities and to look and listen more closely to nature. A sculptural ear is mounted onto the red silhouette of a rose petal, borrowed from the work of Columbia-born, Venezuela-based artist Roberto Obregoń. Nearby, a flag of yellow roses hangs from a flagpole that has been fabricated from a branch. events.title: Out of Bounds at The Kreeger Museum
events.description: Hamiltonian Artists and The Kreeger Museum are pleased to present Out of Bounds, an exhibition of the work of seven Hamiltonian Artists Alumni (Selin Balci, Larry W. Cook, Joyce Yu-Jean Lee, Christie Neptune, Allison Spence, Kyle Tata, and Jing (Ellen) Xu) on view at The Kreeger Museum from October 15 through December 31, 2026. Borrowed from the language of sport, Out of Bounds refers to the space beyond the limits of play. Figuratively, it can describe actions, ideas, or behaviors that go against accepted rules or expectations. Working across painting, photo, sculpture, video, and installation, the artists presented in Out of Bounds consider what it means to question, cross, or redraw established boundaries. The Hamiltonian alumni’s work will be exhibited alongside selected contemporary works from The Kreeger Museum's permanent collection, including artists Sam Gilliam, Frank Stella, Simmie Knox, and William Christenberry. Each of these artists was an iconoclast in their day, rejecting rigid geometries and traditional methods of paint application, and pushing the limits of fine art mediums and subject matter. The Hamiltonian alumni bring a similar spirit of ingenuity to their anti-disciplinary practices—experimenting with materials and challenging conventions of figuration and representation. Some may argue that boundaries exist to be dismantled; as so often, they are imposed to include and to exclude. This exhibition invites the viewer to reconsider who gets to define the rules, and who has the power to enforce them. What is at stake when boundaries are crossed? What becomes possible on the other side of spontaneity and risk? Each artist featured in Out of Bounds approaches these questions through acts of disruption and reimagining, pointing toward the vast possibilities that emerge when established structures are tested. events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California
events.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts
events.address: 1250 New York Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20005
events.description: Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California September 18, 2026 to January 17, 2027 This landmark exhibition of over 80 quilted objects that traces how Black women leaving the Jim Crow South stitched a legacy of survival, connection, and resilience across generations. Routed West features work by more than 70 artists spanning 120 years. The show tells a uniquely American story through quilts from the Second Great Migration, a mass movement of five million African Americans from the rural South to cities in the North and West, to today. Many of those who migrated in search of a more equitable life carried quilts—for warmth and protection, as well as emblems of ancestral memory and cultural survival. Routed West traces the flow and flourishing of quilts in the context of the Second Great Migration, a mass movement of approximately five million African Americans from the rural South to cities in the North and West between 1940 and 1970 in search of a more equitable life. Many of the hundreds of thousands of migrants who arrived in California carried quilts for warmth and protection, as containers for ancestral memory, and as emblems of cultural survival. Organized across several themes through more than 80 artworks with kaleidoscopic patterns, colors, and forms, Routed West offers a history of art through quilts’ joyful power in Black life. The quilts in the exhibition highlight artistic approaches such as repurposing work clothes, improvisational piecing, pattern-based quilting, and tying, practiced by those who would carry these works out of the South. Quilts by migrants from Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, and Texas, regions heavily represented in the westward movement of African Americans, reflect the ways in which these works become cherished heirlooms. events.title: Shifting Boundaries: Perspectives on American Landscapes
events.address: Jefferson Drive at 12th St., SW, Washington, DC
events.description: American painters Willard Metcalf, Dwight Tryon, Winslow Homer, and Abbott Thayer created profoundly beautiful views of the New England landscapes where they lived and worked. These paintings largely depict that environment as timeless and static. Shifting Boundaries looks at these works from a new angle by engaging a multiplicity of voices and viewpoints to explore what these paintings can tell us about changes to this region both past and present. As Shifting Boundaries reveals, the views these artists created of pasturelands in Massachusetts and of seascapes in Maine were transforming even as these artists recorded them. This reshaping of landscapes has only accelerated in the century since Metcalf, Tryon, Homer, and Thayer depicted them. Shifting Boundaries pilots a new mode of collaborative curatorial practice. NMAA Lunder Curator of American Art Diana Greenwold , curatorial assistant Mary Mulcahy , and interpretation specialists Liz Gardner and Amy Freesun partnered with Lauren Brandes (Smithsonian Gardens), Dennis Chestnut (Groundwork Anacostia River DC), Jerome Foster II (Waic Up), Elizabeth James-Perry (Aquinnah Wampanoag artist), Lorette Picciano (Rural Coalition), Stephanie Toothman (National Park Service), and Melinda Whicher (Smithsonian Gardens) to develop the themes for this exhibition, select works of art, and write object labels. The group’s perspectives, drawn from their individual areas of professional expertise and their own personal experiences, allow us to see new details in these stunning works of art. The landscapes become invitations to explore a century of human impact on New England land and water, the erasure of indigenous histories, and the environmental changes that are altering this region today.

The American Story will be the first and only museum in Washington, DC to use artificial intelligence (AI) to bring each visitor a special, individualized opportunity to explore the records of the American people and engage with American history. This exhibit brings more than two million historic records to life, offering a personalized journey through our nation's past. This new museum experience provides all Americans with a special opportunity to celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.

events.title: The American Story
events.description: The National Archives Museum has opened its new flagship exhibition, The American Story, after a multi-year reimagination of its museum galleries, just in time to celebrate America’s Semiquincentennial. Innovative, engaging, and powered by artificial intelligence, The American Story brings more than two million historic records to life and offers visitors opportunities to personally connect their lives to our nation’s storied past. The American Story immerses guests in an interactive exploration of the people, ideas, and events that shaped 250 years of U.S. history through nine captivating galleries that spotlight categories of records in the National Archives. After selecting the topics of interest through AI- driven portals, visitors will be presented with historical content tailored to their individual interests that they can later revisit online. This exhibit features several dozen historic, original artifacts, documents, patents, and film slips, including: George Washington’s annotated draft Constitution The Louisiana Purchase Treaty Notable patents, including Thomas Edison’s lightbulb, Barbie, and Yoda from Star Wars Declassified records from the Cuban Missile Crisis and UFO sightings The first government sponsored film capturing the Wright Brothers’ test flight State gifts to Presidents, including horseshoes gifted by Queen Elizabeth II to President George H.W. Bush Immediately adjacent to the museum galleries is a reimagined Discovery Center, featuring educational arcade games and a classroom with hands-on civics education activities for children and families.

events.title: The Original Historic Georgetown Walking Tour

This tour covers history, architecture, and the stories of Georgetown's over 200 years of residents. You will see and hear stories of: Chesapeake & Ohio Canal - a waterway through the industrial part of the neighborhood. Old Stone House - oldest residential building in the district, now a National Park site. Homes of Jackie & John F. Kennedy - hear about their time in Georgetown before and after his assassination 18th and 19th Century Homes - learn about the diverse, historic architecture of the houses and the stories of those who have lived here. Look for original firemarks, coal chutes, ironworks, and gas lanterns. Hear stories of the Black Georgetown community, immigrants who shaped the neighborhood, and women who bucked social norms. events.title: To Hear Her Speak: Black Women and Shakespeare
events.address: 201 E Capitol St. SE, Washington, DC 20003
events.description: For centuries, Black women have claimed Shakespeare, reshaping his words to assert their humanity, creativity, and power. To Hear Her Speak brings these voices into focus for the first time. Curated by Dr. Patricia Akhimie, Director of the Folger Institute, this landmark exhibition explores the histories of Black women in Shakespearean performance and highlights the ways in which Black women have engaged Shakespeare’s language, stories, and characters in their work. To Hear Her Speak also builds on new research about the presence of Black women in early modern Europe, and shows how they were represented (and misrepresented) by artists and writers of the day, including Shakespeare, whose Sonnet 130 inspired the exhibition’s title. Nearly 100 objects ranging from photographs, playbills, posters, books, diaries, illustrations, and costumes draw from the Folger collection as well as key loans. Together, they document the stories of Maya Angelou, Toni Morrison, Lorraine Hansberry, Mae Turner, Esther Rolle, Phillis Wheatley, and many others. To Hear Her Speak invites visitors to listen closely to the Black women who have used Shakespeare to shape careers, challenge exclusion, and insist upon their place in history. As actors, scholars, authors, artists, musicians, directors, and so much more—Black women have spoken Shakespeare’s words into new possibilities.

events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

events.title: We Make History
events.description: As the nation commemorates 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, "We Make History" explores how history happens, is preserved and shared. In Washington, D.C. and places around the country, many people were quietly keeping the records, building the collections, and developing the skills that would create America’s historical narrative. These community-based stories serve as the building blocks for 250 years of American history. Using the country’s anniversary as a milestone, the museum uses its community driven practice to celebrate local civic engagement and encourage local history keeping. This exhibition is a tribute to celebrating our communities and making possible a better understanding of our shared past. These stories are important to marking the Semiquincentennial because they help show the legacy of how people make history one act, one document, one story at a time. By bringing these stories to the forefront in 2026, the exhibit inspires the next generation to keep and share their own stories and records to add to America’s historical narrative. We Make History has an anticipated opening date of May 30, 2026.

In this interactive workshop, participants will explore these questions through a playful, Mad Libs-style myth-making game. Each participant will receive a take-home workbook filled with creative prompts to help invent an original character, creature, or personal guide. events.description: Founded in 1970, Canadian Brass helped bring the brass quintet to a wide audience with performances that pair polished chamber musicianship with an inviting, conversational spirit. Its expansive repertoire moves from Renaissance and Baroque works to Scott Joplin ragtime, Gershwin, jazz and Broadway, often through inventive arrangements and new commissions. The ensemble’s more than 130 recordings include Stars & Stripes: Canadian Brass Salute America, which reached No. 2 on Billboard’s Classical chart, and Take the “A” Train, a Grammy-nominated album. The appeal lies in hearing five brass players shift effortlessly between musical worlds while making the craft feel lively and close at hand.

And if those instruments are played by Canadian Brass, there is even greater cause for celebration” (Toronto Star). This performance is appropriate for all ages. events.title: Catch Your Breath
events.description: Catch Your Breath is a rising rock band that has quickly gained attention for its emotionally powerful blend of alternative metal, hard rock, post-hardcore, and melodic modern rock. Their music explores themes of resilience, mental health, heartbreak, healing, and self-discovery, creating an authentic connection with listeners who appreciate both emotional vulnerability and hard-hitting musicianship. Catch Your Breath has earned acclaim for energetic live performances that showcase the band's tight chemistry, dynamic stage presence, and ability to recreate the intensity of its studio recordings in concert. As the band continues to expand its catalog and tour alongside some of modern rock's biggest names, Catch Your Breath is establishing itself as one of the most exciting emerging acts in today's heavy music scene.

events.description: Welcome the holidays with Watermark's Christmas in the Capital Tour: Annapolis Traditions and State House Trees. Hear holiday traditions of times past and present as you walk by colonial mansions, Victorian homes, and quaint shops A highlight of the tour is the Maryland State House, with decorated Christmas trees representing the different counties of Maryland, presented by the Federated Garden Clubs of Maryland. The tour ends at Annapolis's grand Christmas tree at Market House Park. Take home the holiday cheer with a goody bag of treats including George Washington’s famed eggnog recipe!

events.description: Gather your family and friends and experience the joy of the holiday season with a festive tour of the William Paca House! Learn how the Paca household prepared to welcome friends and guests for the holidays. At the conclusion of the tour, enjoy a sweet treat, and a take-home recipe to help bring a taste of the past to your own holiday celebrations. Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in November and December. To see times, visit our November and December event calendar . Accessibility Considerations : Accessing the interior of the William Paca House requires ascending and descending several flights of stairs. On this tour of approximately 90 minutes, one of our trained docents will share with you the stories of some of Congressional’s interred residents while walking the beautiful and scenic cemetery grounds. events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California
events.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts
events.address: 1250 New York Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20005
events.description: Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California September 18, 2026 to January 17, 2027 This landmark exhibition of over 80 quilted objects that traces how Black women leaving the Jim Crow South stitched a legacy of survival, connection, and resilience across generations. Routed West features work by more than 70 artists spanning 120 years. The show tells a uniquely American story through quilts from the Second Great Migration, a mass movement of five million African Americans from the rural South to cities in the North and West, to today. Many of those who migrated in search of a more equitable life carried quilts—for warmth and protection, as well as emblems of ancestral memory and cultural survival. Routed West traces the flow and flourishing of quilts in the context of the Second Great Migration, a mass movement of approximately five million African Americans from the rural South to cities in the North and West between 1940 and 1970 in search of a more equitable life. Many of the hundreds of thousands of migrants who arrived in California carried quilts for warmth and protection, as containers for ancestral memory, and as emblems of cultural survival. Organized across several themes through more than 80 artworks with kaleidoscopic patterns, colors, and forms, Routed West offers a history of art through quilts’ joyful power in Black life. The quilts in the exhibition highlight artistic approaches such as repurposing work clothes, improvisational piecing, pattern-based quilting, and tying, practiced by those who would carry these works out of the South. Quilts by migrants from Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, and Texas, regions heavily represented in the westward movement of African Americans, reflect the ways in which these works become cherished heirlooms. events.title: SILENT FILM Series: Wings (1927)
events.description: Soar into the spectacle and emotion of Wings , the first film to ever win the Academy Award for Best Picture. Set against the backdrop of World War I, this drama follows two young fighter pilots whose rivalry, friendship, and love for the same woman unfold amid the danger and excitement of aerial combat. Featuring astonishing flight photography and large-scale action sequences that still inspire and awe nearly a century later, Wings combines thrilling adventure with heartfelt human drama. STARS: Clara Bowm Richard Arlen, Charles Rogers, Gary Cooper RUNTIME: 114 Minutes GENRE: Silent, Action, Drama, Romance, War RATING: PG-13 This show is part of the Silent Film Series , celebrating timeless scores and classic films. When the lights go down and the Mighty Wurlitzer rises from the orchestra pit, audiences are treated to a live organ performance featuring Tedde Gibson—complete with a short musical set before the credits roll and a brief introduction to each silent film. Our beloved Wurlitzer turns 100 this December, having filled the theater with music for nearly a century. The Weinberg Center , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers a historic backdrop for a unique film experience.

events.title: The Grateful Allman Band Experience
events.description: 9pm • $20 • On Eventbrite The Grateful Allman Band Experience Celebrating the Summer of Love All Year Long! The music of The Grateful Dead, The Allman Brothers Band, and The Band The Grateful Allman Band Experience (GABE) celebrates the music of the Grateful Dead, the Allman Brothers Band, and the Band—three legendary acts united by the spirit of the iconic Watkins Glen Summer Jam. Featuring musicians from Mid-Atlantic favorites Danger Bird, Covered with Jam, Montgomery Warlocks, and the Crimestoppers, GABE delivers an improvisation-driven show built on adventurous jams, musical chemistry, and timeless songs. For more than a decade, GABE has entertained audiences from the Carolinas to New Jersey, with multiple recent sellouts drawing crowds of 200–350+. This isn’t a costumed tribute act—it’s a celebration of the feel, freedom, and interplay that made these bands legendary, welcoming jam-band devotees and casual fans alike. For venues, GABE offers three passionate fan bases in one compelling broader promotional reach, a multigenerational audience, and a proven draw.

events.description: The Manhattans featuring Gerald Alston bring the smooth harmonies and soulful storytelling of a group whose roots stretch back to 1962. Alston joined as lead singer in 1970, fronting the band through a defining run of hits, including the chart-topping ballad “Kiss and Say Goodbye” and the Grammy-winning “Shining Star.” Their catalog also includes “There’s No Me Without You” and “It Feels So Good to Be Loved So Bad,” songs that balance tender vocals with richly arranged R&B. The appeal lies in hearing these enduring melodies carried by the voice that helped make them classics.

events.title: The National Mall Architecture Walking Tour
events.address: Basse of the Washington Monument 2 15th St NW, Washington, DC 20024
events.description: Explore Washington’s most famous monuments and memorials from a fresh perspective. This guided walking tour of the National Mall delves beyond the landmarks to reveal how and why they were constructed. Using architecture and design as our lens, we dive into the powerful stories, historical context, and creative decisions that shaped America’s monumental core. From Pierre L’Enfant’s visionary city plan to bold architectural innovations and contentious design debates, discover the drama and meaning embedded in every stone, statue, and landmark. Whether you’re a first-time visitor or a local who’s walked the Mall a hundred times, this tour will give you a new way to see and understand the heart of the city. Meet your guide at the base of the Washington Monument on the North side (the side facing the White House). The tour takes about 2 hours and covers approximately 1 mile, ending at the Lincoln Memorial. This walking tour is also available for private groups on foot or by car or coach. Visit www.dcdesigntours.com to learn more and sign up.

events.address: Warner Theatre - DC 13th and E Streets NW, (between E & F Sts.), Washington, DC 20004
events.description: Set on Christmas Eve in 1882 Georgetown, The Washington Ballet’s The Nutcracker gives Tchaikovsky’s beloved holiday ballet a distinctly American spin. Choreographed by Septime Webre, this version turns George Washington into Clara’s Nutcracker Prince and reimagines the Rat King as King George III. After a battle with toy soldiers, Clara journeys through an enchanted winter to a springtime of cherry blossoms, where Lady Liberty, John Paul Jones, cardinals and frontier dancers join the celebration. First staged by the company in 1961, this festive blend of classic ballet and playful historical touches makes the familiar tale feel rooted in a particular place and imagination.

events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

events.title: Tuba Christmas
events.description: Christmas…Tuba-style Merry Tubachristmas® will celebrate its 52nd year. Created by Harvey Phillips, Merry Tubachristmas® 2026 concerts will be presented in over 300 cities throughout the United States and in several foreign countries. Tubachristmas® is an annual event created to honor Dr. Harvey G. Phillips’ teacher, mentor, friend, and associate, the late great tubist William J. Bell. Every Tubachristmas® performance features traditional Christmas carols especially arranged by American composer Alec Wilder. Through Wilder, Tubachristmas® concerts pay tribute to composers who have embraced these noble instruments with solo and ensemble compositions. It’s no wonder why the warm toned, smooth organ sounds of the tuba-euphonium choir has won the ears and hearts of every audience, making a Tubachristmas® concert an established Christmas tradition in cities throughout the world Learn more about Tubachristmas® at their official website .

events.title: Vintage China Cake Stand Workshop
events.description: Downtown Leesburg’s Most Nostalgic Creative Experience Step inside a beautifully restored historic building in the heart of downtown Leesburg and take part in a hands-on workshop that turns timeless china into a memory you can take home. events.title: Weekend Unwind: Sound Bath + Reiki : Saturday Mornings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Most people start their Saturday with a list. Groceries, errands, the thing they didn't finish on Friday, still buzzing around in their head. By the time they've “relaxed,” it's Sunday night. Weekend Unwind flips that. Eleven o'clock, one hour, lying down. Crystal singing bowls, a short guided meditation, and Reiki, in a small room with ten people in it and no agenda at all. Nothing to achieve, nothing to be good at. You just lie there and let the week drain out of your shoulders. This class has a different feel from our Thursday night one. Thursday is about switching off. Saturday is slower. People arrive less wound up, settle in faster, and tend to float out rather than rush out. Several regulars come as their standing Saturday thing, the way other people have a standing brunch. It pairs well with brunch afterwards, for the record. If you've never been to a sound bath: you keep your clothes on, you lie on a mat under a blanket, you close your eyes, and I do the rest. The bowls are played around and near you, the sound is physical as much as it is musical, you feel it in your chest, and an hour passes faster than you expect. Everything is provided. Show up in something comfortable with ten minutes to spare, and that's the whole preparation. I'm Victoria Vita. I've been a CPA for over twenty years and a healer for more than seven, and I teach every one of these classes myself. When you come back, and most people do, it's the same room, the same bowls, and the same person. That sameness is kind of the point. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Guests mention the warm welcome, feeling comfortable from the first visit, and booking again — that's the Saturday I try to run. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket and bolster provided... just bring yourself • Ten spots only, so the room stays quiet and unhurried • A slow finish... no one is hustled out the door at noon Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

A Tribute to John Lodge - An Evening of Moody Blues Magic
events.description: John Lodge was the legendary bass player, songwriter, and vocalist of Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees The Moody Blues. As the songwriter of mega Moody Blues hits including “Ride My See-Saw,” “I’m Just A Singer (In A Rock and Roll Band),” “Isn’t Life Strange,” and more, Lodge performed and recorded with The Moody Blues for more than five decades, selling in excess of 70 million albums worldwide. Following his sad passing in October last year, his son-in-law Jon Davison (of YES), long-term collaborator Alan Hewitt (keyboards for The Moody Blues band), and his daughter Emily came together to create a unique concert to honor John, his life, and the iconic music of The Moody Blues - with the goal to touch hearts, spread happiness, and celebrate what John always described as “the soundtrack of his life.” The premiere in July captured a rare magic by seamlessly weaving archival vocals and footage of John into a live set performed by the musicians who had been by his side for the last ten years. Earning both rave critical reviews and ecstatic fan acclaim, this breathtaking technical feat created an incredibly powerful, spiritual atmosphere where it was as if John were performing in perfect harmony with his band. Attendees described it as having “amazing sound, lights, and live performances,” and calling it “a masterstroke, very emotional & unforgettable.” Continuing in how John's tours honored all of his bandmates, Jon Davison will bring his beautiful, soaring vocals to legendary songs such as "Nights in White Satin" and "Tuesday Afternoon." The show also includes tributes to Ray Thomas and Mike Pinder, together with the stunning video of Graeme Edge reciting "Late Lament" - which he originally recorded for John so that he could always be on stage beside him. John always wanted audiences to leave his shows with joy in their hearts - and that is exactly what this show delivers. events.description: Acorn and nut collection will take place from September 1 to October 11, 2026. All collections must be dropped off at our "Acorn Station" at the Fairfax City Composting Center (10455 Armstrong St) by the end of that Sunday to ensure donation to the Virginia Department of Forestry on Monday, October 12. Each year, the Virginia Department of Forestry collects a variety of species of acorns and nuts that can be planted at its Augusta Nursery to grow into tree seedlings. Certain nuts can be difficult to find regionally, and availability changes year to year. Without the help of volunteers and local seed collection efforts, it's not possible to fill the demand for tree planting projects across the state. That's why the City of Fairfax needs your help to collect seeds this fall. If you're a private property owner in Fairfax City (such as a homeowner, HOA, religious institution, or commercial property manager) who would like to allow volunteers or staff to collect acorns or nuts on your property, please fill out this form. Filling out the form is not a guarantee seed collection will take place on your property. Fairfax City Seed Collection Map, the iNaturalist app, or a field guide, such as this one for oaks: Field Guide to Native Oak Species of Eastern North America. For acorn identification help, check out the Virginia Department of Forestry's Acorn and Nut Identification Guide.

events.description: Cleveland Park , dubbed The Queen of the Washington Suburbs in 1903, is one of DC’s most picturesque and architecturally eclectic neighborhoods. The neighborhood, once rolling farmland and a breezy summer escape for Washington’s elite, grew into a thriving streetcar suburb lined with fanciful Queen Anne, stately Colonial Revival, and striking early modernist homes. President Grover Cleveland, who the neighborhood is named for, summered here, and the towering Washington National Cathedral still commands the skyline from its hilltop perch. On this walking tour, we’ll hear about the fascinating history of the second-largest cathedral in the country and explore its charming grounds. We’ll wind through Cleveland Park’s shady streets and uncover how architecture, landscape, and a carefully crafted community identity shaped this neighborhood into one of Washington’s most desirable addresses. Meet your guide outside the main entrance to the Washington National Cathedral, near the glass elevators. This tour-hour tours covers about 1 mile and concludes near the intersection of Wisconsin Avenue and Idaho Avenue NW. Private versions are also available—on foot, by car, or by coach. Visit www.dcdesigntours.com to learn more and reserve your spot.

events.title: Congressional Cemetery Introductory Tour
events.description: Over 67,000 people are interred at Congressional Cemetery, ranging from 1807 all the way until the present day. Their stories are American history in microcosm, all in 35 acres of the nation’s capital. Come and experience their extraordinary lives in a one of kind portal into the past. On this tour of approximately 90 minutes, one of our trained docents will share with you the stories of some of Congressional’s interred residents while walking the beautiful and scenic cemetery grounds. Tickets are only $5 and all proceeds go to benefitting our non-profit mission of historical preservation and education. This is a non-refundable donation. Please come prepared with comfortable and weather-appropriate clothing and shoes, as the tours often stray from the main paths. Tours are rain or shine. Visitors may meet docents at the front gate of the cemetery located at the corner of E St. and Potomac Ave. The cemetery is closed to dogs on Saturdays from 11am – 3pm. Purchase Tickets Here!

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.title: Georgetown Architecture Walking Tour
events.address: 1056 Thomas Jefferson St NW, Washington, DC 20007
events.description: Founded more than 50 years before Washington became the capital, Georgetown began as a gritty port town on the banks of the Potomac. Though it was once dismissed by First Lady Abigail Adams as a “dirty little hole,” today Georgetown is one of DC’s most charming and sought-after neighborhoods. Cobblestone streets lined with colorful rowhouses, elegant churches, and grand mansions tell the story of centuries of change. Our tour explores Georgetown’s evolution from working-class waterfront to wealthy ward, tracing how architecture, commerce, and culture reshaped the neighborhood over centuries. Along the way, we’ll explore hidden alleys, appreciate impressive architectural landmarks, and discuss storied estates. This is Georgetown as you’ve never seen it—perfect for lovers of design, history, and intrigue. Meet your guide at the intersection of Thomas Jefferson Street NW and the C&O Canal. This 2.5 hour walking tour covers about 2.5 miles and ends at Georgetown Waterfront Park near 33rd St and Water Street. Private versions are also available—on foot, by car, or by coach. Visit www.dcdesigntours.com to learn more and reserve your spot.

events.title: Georgetown Spy Tour with a Former CIA Officer
events.description: Explore the hidden history of this iconic neighborhood with a former CIA officer. If you enjoy real-life spy stories, covert operations, and international intrigue, this fun, educational and interactive tour is for you. Visit select spy sites in the iconic Georgetown neighborhood. Along the way your expert guide, and former intelligence officer, shares personal anecdotes from their time overseas and interprets the remarkable history shaped by the people who called this neighborhood home, including leaders, heroes and traitors. Learn about the unique mindset of this profession as you explore the hidden histories that residents played in espionage during WWII and the Cold War. Hear more about impersonal communication and how it mitigates against risk and test the theory by reading a signal site and unloading a dead drop. Don’t forget your walking shoes, bring water, and dress for the weather. *Note: This tour begins outside of Oak Hill Cemetery and ends about .7 mile away outside of Martin's Tavern. Not seeing a tour on the calendar that works for your schedule? Submit a request for a new date/time and we'll work with you and do our best to accommodate your needs. Private tours available upon request in English, Spanish, French, Russian, Turkish, Hebrew or Arabic. Our Hosts: Rosanna Minchew has 20+ years of experience in intelligence, security, and risk, including 15 years at CIA in operational and leadership positions in Latin America, Europe, South Asia, Iraq and Washington D.C. Today, Rosanna continues to participate in scenario-based training in the intelligence space, has advised on interdiction efforts by U.S. Customs & Border Protection, and has been integral in insider risk investigations in the oil and energy sector. George: A former Senior National Security Officer with 30 years of experience with the Central Intelligence Agency, Department of State, and as a Military Intelligence Officer in the United States Army. events.title: Kinnfolk at the Old Brogue
events.description: Old Brogue Irish Pub welcomes Kinnfolk on Saturday, November 29th, 2026 in Great Falls, Fairfax County, Virginia. Hailing from Roanoke, Virginia, the husband-and-wife duo of Josh and Julie Kinn weave octave mandolin, bodhrán (Irish drum), and smooth vocal harmonies into their Celtic folk music from the heart of the Blue Ridge Mountains. These young musicians have received well-deserved accolades from Celtic media and have performed extensively throughout the Eastern U.S. and Canada. They were awarded a grant from the National Endowment for the Arts for their project "Star Above the Mountain," a body of work exploring the history, geography, and folk legends of their town. This performance celebrates authentic Appalachian heritage, intimate musicianship, and heartfelt Celtic traditions in Fairfax County, Virginia. Admission is $25 plus tax per performance; full six-concert season tickets are $135 plus tax. Kinnfolk delivers soulful instrumentation, beautiful harmonies, and the spirit of Blue Ridge folk music. events.title: Leanna Firestone
events.description: Leanna Firestone is a Nashville, Tennessee based singer songwriter and multi instrumentalist known for candid, diaristic indie pop. Her songs often draw from uncomfortable memories, awkward moments, and personal experiences, pairing confessional lyrics with acoustic driven production. She began building an audience during the pandemic by sharing original music on TikTok while studying Commercial Songwriting at Middle Tennessee State University. In 2021, her song “Strawberry Mentos” gained traction on the platform, becoming the lead single of her debut EP, Y/N, which has since gained tens of millions of streams across platforms. Firestone has continued to release music steadily, including her album Forward / Slash (2022), the EPs Public Displays of Affection and Good Grief (2023), and fan-favorite single “Becoming Unbecoming” (2024). In 2025, she released her live EP An Evening with Leanna Firestone (Acoustic at The Deli) and toured with Natasha Bedingfield. Her latest album, The Answer, featuring the lead single “Victory Lap, ” was released in May 2026, followed by the first leg of her headline tour across the US and Toronto. With the first half of the tour now complete, Leanna’s second “lap” is set to begin in November 2026. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

Follow Jean-Valjean from his beginnings as convict #24601 to life in hiding, to protector of Cosette, pursued all the while by the relentless Javert, culminating in the revolutionary passions of the 1832 Paris uprising. Featuring: Kevin S. events.description: Discover Frederick’s Past as we Navigate through the Labyrinth of Graves, Crypts and Monuments of Historic Mount Olivet Cemetery. One of Maryland’s Largest and most Beautiful Cemeteries. Final Resting Place of Francis Scott Key, Author of our National Anthem, the Star Spangled Banner; Maryland's first Governor, Thomas Johnson and Civil War Heroine, Barbara Fritchie. Tour also includes Intriguing Facts about the Cemetery’s Origin, Tombstone Design, Grave Robbing, Mass Graves, plus stops at other Distinctive Burial Plots, including Revolutionary War, War of 1812 and Civil War. Tour concludes with a visit to the Key Memorial Chapel. Reservations Required. (This is Not a Ghost Tour)

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Nutcracker Magical Christmas Ballet
events.address: 7750 Capital One Tower Rd, Tysons, VA 22102
events.description: Nutcracker! Magical Christmas Ballet is a dazzling holiday production that reimagines Tchaikovsky's beloved classic with world-class ballet, breathtaking scenery, elaborate costumes, and spectacular theatrical effects. Featuring an international cast of accomplished dancers, the performance combines classical choreography with imaginative storytelling, transporting audiences through Clara's enchanting journey into a magical world filled with toy soldiers, dancing snowflakes, and the unforgettable Kingdom of Sweets. Lavish sets, larger-than-life puppetry, soaring acrobatics, and innovative stage illusions enhance the timeless score, creating a visually stunning experience that appeals to both longtime ballet enthusiasts and first-time theatergoers. While honoring the traditions that have made The Nutcracker a cherished holiday favorite for generations, the production introduces fresh artistic elements that add excitement and wonder to every performance. With its blend of exceptional dance, memorable music, and festive holiday magic, Nutcracker! Magical Christmas Ballet has become an annual tradition for families seeking an unforgettable seasonal celebration.

events.title: State Champs
events.description: State Champs is a pop-punk band celebrated for its infectious energy, hook-filled songwriting, and high-octane live performances that have made it a leading force in modern rock. Formed in Albany, New York, the group quickly gained recognition with acclaimed albums such as The Finer Things, Around the World and Back, Living Proof, and Kings of the New Age, blending punchy guitar riffs, soaring choruses, and emotionally resonant lyrics into a signature sound. Fronted by vocalist Derek DiScanio, State Champs crafts songs that explore friendship, relationships, personal growth, and perseverance while maintaining the upbeat spirit that defines the genre. Their concerts are renowned for nonstop audience participation, energetic sing-alongs, and an undeniable chemistry that transforms every performance into a celebration of pop-punk culture. Through relentless touring, consistently strong releases, and an unwavering commitment to authentic songwriting, State Champs has earned its place among the most respected and influential bands in today's pop-punk scene.

events.title: Static Dress
events.description: Static Dress is a British post-hardcore band that pairs jagged, heavy guitars and urgent vocals with big melodic hooks and a carefully built visual world. Their 2021 EP, Prologue... (Comic Book Soundtrack), introduced an unfolding story told through music and comic-book lore; the following year, debut album Rouge Carpet Disaster widened their sound across emo, screamo, metal, pop and electronic influences. Tracks such as “clean.” and “such.a.shame” capture the push between abrasion and melody, while “Lye solution” brings in collaborators from Loathe, BVDLVD and Hail the Sun. The result gives their music both a cathartic punch and a vivid sense of narrative.

events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

Moving away from the commercial look of the modern holiday, we will focus on the rich diversity of “The Winter Field”—utilizing layered evergreens, architectural dried elements, and the “saved” treasures of late autumn. What You’ll Explore: The Power of Texture: Learn to layer multiple varieties of cedar, pine, and fir for a lush, professional-grade base. The Dried Garden: Integrating natural elements like seed pods, dried citrus, red chilis and flowers for a modern take on the “Nature-First” aesthetic. Organic Mechanics: Mastering the traditional wire-wrap technique to ensure your wreath stays fresh and secure through the season.

events.title: Georgetown Spy Tour with a Former CIA Officer
events.description: Explore the hidden history of this iconic neighborhood with a former CIA officer. If you enjoy real-life spy stories, covert operations, and international intrigue, this fun, educational and interactive tour is for you. Visit select spy sites in the iconic Georgetown neighborhood. Along the way your expert guide, and former intelligence officer, shares personal anecdotes from their time overseas and interprets the remarkable history shaped by the people who called this neighborhood home, including leaders, heroes and traitors. Learn about the unique mindset of this profession as you explore the hidden histories that residents played in espionage during WWII and the Cold War. Hear more about impersonal communication and how it mitigates against risk and test the theory by reading a signal site and unloading a dead drop. Don’t forget your walking shoes, bring water, and dress for the weather. *Note: This tour begins outside of Oak Hill Cemetery and ends about .7 mile away outside of Martin's Tavern. Not seeing a tour on the calendar that works for your schedule? Submit a request for a new date/time and we'll work with you and do our best to accommodate your needs. Private tours available upon request in English, Spanish, French, Russian, Turkish, Hebrew or Arabic. Our Hosts: Rosanna Minchew has 20+ years of experience in intelligence, security, and risk, including 15 years at CIA in operational and leadership positions in Latin America, Europe, South Asia, Iraq and Washington D.C. Today, Rosanna continues to participate in scenario-based training in the intelligence space, has advised on interdiction efforts by U.S. Customs & Border Protection, and has been integral in insider risk investigations in the oil and energy sector. George: A former Senior National Security Officer with 30 years of experience with the Central Intelligence Agency, Department of State, and as a Military Intelligence Officer in the United States Army. events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. events.title: CCAS Academy: The Hidden Life of Plastics: What's Really in Our Water?
events.description: What happens to plastic after it enters our environment? Join GW Assistant Professor of Chemistry Lauren Pincus for an exploration of microplastics and their growing presence in our waterways. Drawing on current scientific research‚ Lauren will examine how microplastics enter aquatic environments‚ interact with environmental contaminants‚ and what scientists are learning about their potential long-term effects on ecosystems and human health. Through an introduction to her laboratory’s research and an inside look at some of its fascinating findings‚ attendees will learn how scientists collect‚ process‚ and analyze environmental samples to better understand the presence and impact of microplastics. Lauren will also demonstrate how researchers investigate these tiny particles and uncover what they reveal about the health of our waterways. About the Speaker Dr. Pincus’ research aims to examine complexation of inorganic pollutants by natural and engineered solids using advanced synchrotron spectroscopy techniques in order to understand and control the fate and transport of inorganic pollutants in the environment‚ develop novel sustainable and selective materials for aqueous contaminant removal‚ and design new technologies for climate change mitigation.

events.title: Cherish the Ladies
events.description: For four decades, Cherish the Ladies has been a leading ensemble in Irish traditional music, known for performances that combine instrumental virtuosity, vocals, and step dance. Led by Joanie Madden—a flute and whistle player and National Endowment for the Arts National Heritage Fellow—the Grammy-nominated group has released 18 albums, toured internationally, and collaborated with symphony orchestras. This holiday season, the ensemble presents its Celtic Christmas program, featuring arrangements of traditional carols including “Angels We Have Heard on High,” “The First Noel,” and “Silent Night.” Drawing on a repertoire developed across several holiday recordings— On Christmas Night , A Star in the East , and Christmas in Ireland —the performance highlights Celtic instrumentation, vocal harmonies, and step dancing, with guest vocalists and dancers joining throughout. The concert features Madden alongside Mirella Murray (accordion), Nollaig Casey (fiddle), Hannah Collins (piano), Mary Coogan (guitar), and Cheryl Prashker (percussion), joined by vocalists and guitarists Kate Purcell, Don Stiffe, and Bruce Foley. Step dancers James Greenan, Tyler Schwartz, Joe Harrison, and Nathan Pilatzke complete the program, bringing together music, song, and dance in a performance rooted in Irish tradition.
